dse_runs.notes: Tight accuracy spec: max_abs_err <= 2^-20 (~9.54e-7) at >=50 MSPS. Precision comes from data width and iteration count, not from unrolling; area is the primary objective (min luts_plus_ffs) with power_index secondary. Prefer small-width iterative/pipelined families with enough fractional bits; avoid large unroll factors that inflate LUTs. Ensure the front is well spread and feasible on both constraints.

final_text: The `high_precision` spec is finalized. L1: `run_dse` consumed the entire 400-evaluation budget (4 rounds — map_front ×3 then stop) and produced a single feasible, non-dominated design, `pipelined_m:data_width=27,n_iter=22,angle_guard=0,frac_guard=0,rounding=trunc,m=7`, with luts_plus_ffs=2340 (luts=1930, ffs=410), power_index=4.4, throughput_msps=52 and max_abs_err=7.54e-07 (2^-20.34) — comfortably inside both constraints (≥50 MSPS, ≤9.53674e-07). L2: the spec has no system scenario, so `simulate_system` only contributed simulated DDS facts (SFDR 142.3 dBc, SNR 130.5 dB, 6-cycle contract latency, 1-cycle initiation interval) and left the selection unchanged. L3/L4/L5 (run via the `ladder` subagent): `verify_rtl` had no recorded row for this design (a fresh exhaustive W=27 run is too heavy live), `synthesize` had no recorded synthesis row, and `back_annotate` reported `no_measured_data` — no winner change was flagged, so no `reexplore` was needed. The spec was finalized on the min-luts_plus_ffs rule with the design above; note that all cost figures (LUTs/FFs/throughput/power) remain cost-model estimates under M1 calibration, while the error figure is exact from the golden model. Memory storage was declined (switched off for this campaign), so no lesson was persisted.
